chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of it, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abū Ḥabīb al-Asadī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying about a man who gets a nosebleed while he is in a state of wudu (ablution): He washes away the traces of the blood and performs salat (prayer).

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man about whom the legal ruling is being asked
key_terms.يَرْعُفُ: has a nosebleed; blood flows from the nose

ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed break wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who experiences a nosebleed while in a state of wudu (ablution). It indicates that he should wash away the traces of blood and then perform salat (prayer), showing that the occurrence of nosebleed itself does not necessitate renewing wudu (ablution).
